text:
anna-support: heads-up — enterprise customer (internal ticket 4521) sees intermittent EventSource streams in Safari. Happens when requests go through our proxy-delegate offload + CDN. They report partial data then stream stalls, client never gets final event and reconnects repeatedly. 😕

jay-eng: can you paste the minimal repro? Safari version? polyfill?

anna-support: Safari 16.4 on macOS and iOS 16.4. No app SW, they tested both native EventSource and a small htmx-based polyfill. Repro steps in their words: 1) open page, 2) connect to /v1/stream with Authorization header bearer token, 3) see 1-3 events, then stop. Chrome works fine.

maya-devx: likely CDN/edge is returning a 304 or caching a chunked response and stripping Authorization on subsequent conditional requests. Safari's EventSource + H2 can be sensitive to 304 mid-stream.

liam-sre: any logs from edge-proxy? deploy-bot, can we pull the proxy logs around ts 2026-07-08T13:12:xx?

deploy-bot: pulled logs. snippet:
```
EDGE PROXY: request /v1/stream 200 chunked
EDGE PROXY: upstream returned 304 after conditional range lookup
EDGE PROXY: auth header missing on cached-hit request
UPSTREAM: stream closed by client (EOF)
```

jay-eng: that matches a hypothesis: our delegate offload caches the initial response, but when the CDN issues conditional GETs (304) our edge path rebuilds a request to origin without Authorization header, causing origin to close or return incomplete frames. Safari sees truncated stream and doesn't reopen properly.

anna-support: customer also notes they saw repeated small reconnections (every ~2s) and sometimes a final empty data frame: `data: \n\n` nothing else.

maya-devx: workaround options for them: 1) disable caching for SSE endpoints (Cache-Control: no-store, private) 2) append short-lived token as query param (not ideal for security) 3) make edge include Authorization in conditional requests / include Vary: Authorization and set cache key to include auth.

jay-eng: triage steps for eng:
- confirm edge proxy behavior on 304 with delegate offload enabled
- check if we strip Authorization on cache-revalidate path
- reproduce locally by configuring our staging CDN to revalidate cached SSE response

liam-sre: I'll run a quick repro: curl client that simulates EventSource (keepalive + chunked), then force a conditional GET from CDN.

liam-sre: quick repro script I used:
```
# origin (python) -> yields SSE every sec
python -m http.server 8000 &
# simulate chunked SSE response:
# curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "http://localhost:8000/stream"
```
(kept it intentionally minimal)

jay-eng: question: is our runtime sending `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and `Connection: keep-alive`? Safari expects a continuous stream; if a 304 occurs mid-stream browser behavior is undefined.

maya-devx: also try `Cache-Control: no-transform` and `Vary: Authorization` to ensure CDN doesn't reinterpret. Some CDNs will gzip or coalesce if not explicit.

anna-support: customer asked whether polyfill matters — they tried a basic eventsource-polyfill and saw same behavior, so likely native Safari quirk + CDN edges.

edge-proxy-bot: alert: delegate-offload feature toggled ON for customer tenant. Config: cache_on_auth=true, revalidate_on_conditional=true, strip_sensitive_headers_on_revalidate=true

jay-eng: aha — strip_sensitive_headers_on_revalidate=true. That's probably the root cause. When CDN sends conditional GET for revalidation we send without Authorization. Origin then treats it as unauth and returns 304 or closes stream. Need to change to preserve auth for SSE endpoints.

liam-sre: immediate mitigation: set customer route to bypass caching for `/v1/stream` and related SSE routes. I'll patch rule in edge-config and roll.

maya-devx: longer term: change default behavior or add config flag to keep Authorization in cache key for endpoints with `Accept: text/event-stream` or `Content-Type: text/event-stream`. Also add a safety rule: never respond 304 to an active streaming connection; force revalidation to origin early.

anna-support: sent customer the temporary workaround (disable caching on stream endpoints). Customer confirmed workaround helps — they now see continuous stream in Safari for ~30 minutes during our test. :thumbsup:

jay-eng: follow-ups:
- (jay-eng) open PR to change strip_sensitive_headers_on_revalidate for SSE routes + add unit test
- (liam-sre) deploy edge-config bypass for tenant and monitor logs for next 48h
- (maya-devx) document SSE caveats with CDN/304 + recommended headers in support KB

maya-devx: KB draft note: required headers for reliable browser SSE across CDNs:
```
Cache-Control: private, no-store, max-age=0
Vary: Authorization
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-transform
```
Also: avoid query param tokens if you need strict auth audits.

anna-support: customer is ok with staged roll and asked for ETA. Jay — can you estimate the PR + rollout?

jay-eng: aim for code + canary in 2 business days, full rollout after smoke in 24h. I'll log the RFC in eng-releases.

liam-sre: I'll keep watch and post any anomalies to this thread.

deploy-bot: edge-config rule patched for tenant (bypass caching) at 2376543345 by liam-sre.

anna-support: thanks everyone. I'll update the customer and close the ticket once we verify 48h clean.

maya-devx: note for future: safari sometimes treats final `\n\n` differently if there are trailing CRLF vs LF; recommend consistent `\n\n` event terminators. small but can affect detection of end-of-message in some polyfills.

jay-eng: adding a test to our E2E harness that runs Safari in CI with a simulated CDN revalidation to catch regressions.

anna-support: closing loop here. If anything pops up ping on #eng-runtime or reopen this thread. :sparkles:
